claims.text: Integrating CALPHAD, ab initio calculations, high-fidelity sampling, and experimental calibration can efficiently predict HEA melting thermodynamics.
The framework can predict melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change at melting, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties.
Errors for the predicted melting properties will be below approximately 10%.
The framework will achieve this performance across the broad compositional space of the HEA family.
CALPHAD-based high-throughput screening, multiscale modeling, and experimental validation can efficiently accelerate HEA materials discovery.
In situ DSC and synchrotron measurements at selected compositions can calibrate and validate the proposed melting-property framework.
Mixing enthalpies, vibrational entropy, and diffusion kinetics govern phase stability and the solid-liquid transition in HEAs.
The combined framework captures configurational and vibrational contributions to the free-energy landscape.
CALPHAD provides multicomponent phase-stability predictions relevant to the framework.
Ab initio calculations and high-fidelity sampling will refine CALPHAD predictions sufficiently to resolve fusion and liquid-state thermodynamic parameters more precisely.
Experimental and theoretical analysis of successful and failed alloy cases can improve the accuracy of a thermodynamic database.
The proposed method will significantly improve upon current high-throughput screening methods.
Existing high-throughput methods mainly estimate melting points and do not fully capture fusion thermodynamics or melting-associated volume changes.
Unexpected inter-element interactions or complex diffusion dynamics may reduce prediction accuracy in some compositions.
Inadequate treatment of high-temperature vibrational effects in the ab initio models may reduce prediction accuracy.
The scalability of the ab initio component across the full HEA compositional space is uncertain.

contradictions.description: The main performance claim says errors will be below or within about 10% across broad HEA composition space, but the falsification rule allows one tested composition to exceed 10% in any property without falsifying the framework. This does not match the breadth of the stated accuracy claim.
